title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-07
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > ZA2 > SoundForge > CD Architect > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a solid 6/7/70 Fillmore West show with standout The Other One and Good Lovin' > Drums > Good Lovin', good‑ish tape quality but occasional bass heaviness and glitches.
ai_review.review: The performance shines especially in the second set – the Cryptical → Drums → The Other One sequence, a smoking Good Lovin' jam, and an inspired New Speedway Boogie.  Reviewers love the acoustic first set and Jerry’s pedal‑steel work, though some note a heavy‑bass mix and occasional tape warble or splice glitches.  Overall the show is considered a must‑listen gem from 1970.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (20+) give 4–5 stars and praise key performances; recording is rated good with minor flaws, yielding a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear soundboard capture with some hissing/tape warble, heavy low‑end bass, and occasional glitches (e.g., splice in Cumberland Blues).  Acoustic set sounds especially clean.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic first set sets a relaxed vibe, then the band launches into an adventurous second set with seamless segues (Cryptical → Drums → The Other One) and a powerful jam through Good Lovin'.  Even the slower‑tempo Sugar Magnolia is noted but not enough to mar the overall flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His voice on New Speedway Boogie gets mixed notes – some love it, others call it strained – but his pedal‑steel work and guitar tone are widely praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: One reviewer mentions Phil’s harmonies sounding off; otherwise no major comments.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir takes lead vocals on Cosmic Charlie (highlighted by a reviewer).
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum breaks, especially the quiet interlude before The Other One and the Good Lovin' > Drums segment, receive strong praise for build‑up and texture.
